730480101.text: How nostalgic. It's been hundreds of years since I last saw such a sight... It's thanks to you that I could see Vanarana's dreamscape again.

730480102.text: Wow! So you're actually that old...?

730480105.text: Is that so? Maybe it's because I've absorbed more memories and knowledge. In Vanarana's dreamscape, there is no day and night. Everything is tranquil and peaceful.

730480106.text: We have long lifespans too, so we have very little concept of time. We measure the passage of time by the growth of trees, the blooming of flowers, the rising of the moon, and so on.

730480107.text: If we are going to have Festival Utsava, we should bear the Bija soon, right?

730480108.text: Yes... Speaking of which, what is a Bija? Araja and Arama didn't explain much about it before.

730480109.text: You have become friends with Aranara, so you should have heard about the principle of the Ararakalari. Do you know of it?

730480110.text: Arana mentioned the power of memory...

730480111.text: Arana, huh? How nostalgic. I hope Arana's alright. A little hotheaded, yes, but I doubt you would have been told about this if that one hadn't considered you a friend.

730480112.text: Bija is a fruit made from extracted dreams and memories — the crystallization of all that is precious to us Aranara. It is a fruit, but it is also a seed of hope.

730480113.text: Bija can help to realize dreams, so long as these dreams are meant to help others. I'm sure that you and the Aranara preparing this Bija do have such wishes, yes?
